title: Frontend request timeouts: use AbortController with setTimeout and clearTimeout, not AbortSignal.timeout, because browserslist includes Chrome 94-102
answers: How should I add a timeout to a fetch call in the MLflow frontend?
Why not use AbortSignal.timeout for a request timeout?
Why does the existing fetchEndpointRaw timeoutMs option leak timers?
body:
Path: mlflow/server/js/src/experiment-tracking/hooks/useServerInfo.tsx:fetchServerInfo is a single-call-site timeout that wraps fetchAPI and passes signal into it; fetchEndpointRaw's timeoutMs option is the existing alternative in the same frontend fetch layer.
Rule: for a per-call deadline, create new AbortController(), arm setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), ms), pass controller.signal, and call clearTimeout in finally. Do not use AbortSignal.timeout, which needs Chrome 103+, while browserslist still resolves chrome 94-102, and_uc 15.5 and op_mob 80. Browser APIs are not polyfilled, so the constraint is real.
Symptom: none recorded for this convention. The PR notes that the existing fetchEndpointRaw timeoutMs path never calls clearTimeout, so copying it duplicates a timer leak.
Constraints: adding timeout support to the widely used fetchAPI was judged an infrastructure change and left for a separate PR; the timeout is therefore hand-rolled at the call site.
applies: Frontend code in mlflow/server/js that needs a per-request timeout on fetch.
says: The web interface crashes on older supported browsers when checking server information.
Why does the server status check fail on older browser or mobile versions?
The web dashboard leaks memory over time because network request timers are not cleared.
Network requests should time out cleanly without breaking compatibility on older browser versions.
Ensure server info requests abort on slow connections without leaking background timers.
search: `mlflow/server/js/src/experiment-tracking/hooks/useServerInfo.tsx:fetchServerInfo` implements per-request timeouts using `AbortController`, `setTimeout`, and `clearTimeout` in a `finally` block when calling `fetchAPI`. `AbortSignal.timeout` must not be used because browserslist includes Chrome 94-102, Android UC 15.5, and Opera Mobile 80, and browser APIs are not polyfilled. The hand-rolled call-site timeout explicitly clears timers to avoid the timer leak present in `fetchEndpointRaw`'s `timeoutMs` implementation. Guidance applies to frontend fetch calls in `mlflow/server/js` requiring request deadlines prior to general timeout support in `fetchAPI`.
